card.title: Touring North
card.comment: North Island enchants with pristine beaches, emerald hills, volcanic landscapes, ancient forests, and spectacular ocean panoramas.

days.day_comment: Our three-day adventure from home towards Raglan, Hamilton and Tauranga started with a pleasantly uneventful drive to Taihape. We stopped for lunch at the Brown Sugar Café before stretching our legs with a walk around the **Mount Stewart Loop**. A good way to break up the journey and get some fresh air before hitting the road again. Our next stop was Te Kūiti for a supermarket visit, although the local roadworks had other ideas. A few unexpected diversions added an extra 20 kilometres to our journey before we finally arrived in Raglan. Dinner was a Turkish kebab, followed by a drive to our accommodation, the **Treehouse** – a quirky little place about 20 kilometres outside Raglan. A rather unusual spot, but certainly something different! The following day was devoted to exploring the Raglan area. First up was the **Bridal Veil Falls** walkway, which turned out to be a real surprise. The spectacular waterfall, plunging 55 metres into a forest-fringed pool, was well worth the visit. In the afternoon, we headed to **Wainui Reserve Bush Park** for another hike, followed by a walk down to the beach through **Bryant Memorial Scenic Reserve**. We then made our way to **Manu Bay** to watch the surfers tackling its legendary left-hand point break. Even for those of us who prefer walking to surfing, it was quite a spectacle. Our final stop was the **Te Toto Gorge** Lookout, offering some magnificent coastal views. The next morning, we headed towards Hamilton and stopped at the **Hamilton Gardens**. What was supposed to be a relatively short visit turned into almost three hours of wandering through an impressive collection of themed gardens. The Japanese Garden, Kitchen Garden, Herb Garden and many other creative spaces kept us entertained far longer than expected. Definitely a place worth visiting – and perhaps allowing more time than originally planned! From Hamilton, we continued to Tauranga, where we made a special stop at the **Tauranga Public Library**. Our daughter-in-law had been involved in its design, so we were particularly interested to see the finished building. It turned out to be a fascinating piece of architecture, with a very interesting design and structure. The day finished with a lovely dinner at a local Thai restaurant with Fiona's brother and her niece. After a good catch-up, we headed to Tauranga Tourist Park for the night, ready to continue our journey further north the following morning.

After escaping the morning rush-hour traffic in Tauranga, we pointed the car towards Colville, ready for two days of exploring the beautiful beaches of the **Coromandel Peninsula**. And what a collection of beaches it turned out to be! Some were old favourites, including Waihi, Whiritoa and Whangamata, while others, such as Opito, Otama and New Chums, were new discoveries for us. Our routine was fairly simple: drive to a beach, get out, enjoy a short walk, admire the scenery and, of course, take plenty of photos. It was hardly an exhausting schedule, although getting in and out of the car so many times probably counted as a reasonable workout! We also squeezed in a little shopping in Whitianga before settling in for the night at Shelly Beach TOP 10 Holiday Park, a lovely spot and a very welcome place to put our feet up. The following day brought more coastal exploring. We enjoyed a walk along Oamaru Bay, treated ourselves to ice creams in Coromandel town and then stretched our legs again on Amodeo Bay beach. Fiona was slightly disappointed that we didn't make it to Tuateawa or Wakawau, but I had reached my limit for driving on gravel roads. There is only so much dust, rattling and concentration one can take in a day! Eventually, we called time on our beach-hopping adventure and continued to Colville, our starting point for the upcoming **Pahi Coastal Walk**. Time to swap the car seats for walking boots!

After wrapping up our walking adventures on the Coromandel Peninsula, we decided it was time for a little break from all that strenuous activity. We spent four days in Auckland, enjoying some well-deserved rest at our friend's place and catching up with family. Eventually, though, the call of the road became too strong, and we headed north to explore a little of **Northland**, using Whau Valley, Whangārei, as our base. 
Our journey started with a stop at **Matakana's** weekend market, an interesting place full of local produce, crafts and all sorts of tempting distractions. From there, we made our way to **Langs Beach**, where we were treated to a rather spectacular show: a large pod of dolphins happily playing in the crystal-clear water. Not a bad way to start the Northland chapter! A short stroll along **Waipū Beach** followed before we continued to our accommodation in Whangārei. But we weren't quite finished exploring for the day. We headed out again towards **Bream Head – Te Whara**, stopping first at Urquharts Bay before opting for the direct walk to **Smugglers Bay**. What a little paradise! An idyllic hideaway with wonderfully clear water, sparkling white sand and beautiful, mature Pōhutukawa trees. It was one of those places where you could easily lose track of time. We eventually dragged ourselves away, returning for a simple dinner and a couple of drinks – a perfectly respectable way to end our first day in Northland. 
The following morning began with a visit to **Whangārei Falls**, another little waterfall gem in the North Island. It made us wonder just how many other natural wonders are hiding around the country, waiting to be discovered. From there, we headed to Matapōuri Beach and enjoyed a slightly longer walk to the gorgeous **Whale Bay**. Our plans to walk all the way to **Tutukākā Lighthouse** were somewhat less successful, as unfavourable tides forced us to cut the walk short, completing only about a third of the intended route. Nature, as usual, had the final say! 
A quick shopping expedition at Pak'nSave, followed by another uncomplicated dinner, brought our little Northland adventure to a close. We hadn't covered huge distances or conquered any particularly challenging tracks, but we had enjoyed beautiful beaches, unexpected wildlife encounters and some lovely coastal scenery. Sometimes, a little bit of exploring and a couple of quiet evenings are exactly what a road trip needs.

Before heading further north, we made a few essential stops in Whangārei for grocery shopping and fuel, and took the opportunity to photograph the striking exterior of the **Hundertwasser Art Centre**. With supplies sorted, we were ready to continue our adventure towards the Far North. 
Our first stop was Opito Bay near Kerikeri, where the low tide worked in our favour and allowed us to walk across to Tikorangi Island. We then continued to Matauri Bay and Te Ngaere Bay, enjoying some lovely coastal scenery along the way. Unfortunately, a few other places on our wish list had to be abandoned, as the access roads turned out to be more suitable for 4WD vehicles than our trusty transport. We settled for stretching our legs on Cable Bay Beach before finally arriving at our temporary home, **Ahipara TOP 10 Holiday Park**. 
The campsite had an interesting mix of visitors, including several cyclists and walkers who were just beginning their mission to conquer the mighty **Te Araroa Trail**. Some had barely got started and were already having to deal with blisters – not exactly the most encouraging introduction to a long-distance adventure! 
The following day was devoted to exploring **Cape Reinga**. We drove all the way to the lighthouse car park and enjoyed the pleasant walk down to the lighthouse, with plenty of photo opportunities and spectacular views where the Tasman Sea meets the Pacific Ocean. On our way back, we stopped at the impressive **Giant Sand Dunes at Te Paki** before heading to **90 Mile Beach** near Hukatere Lodge. 
There we encountered another group of cyclists, although their approach was slightly more comfortable: a support van carried their luggage, leaving them free to tackle the Te Araroa Trail with just day packs. A sensible arrangement, especially considering the terrain! Incidentally, 90 Mile Beach is actually only about 55 miles long. Early settlers apparently overestimated its length, assuming they covered around 30 miles a day on horseback. They hadn't accounted for the soft sand, which slowed their progress considerably. A classic case of optimistic maths! 
The next morning brought an uneventful drive towards Manganui Bluff. We maintained our traditional stop at the Opononi ice cream place for a coffee, then passed through the Waipoua Forest without making the detour to visit the famous Tane Mahuta. Eventually, we reached our next destination along Aranga Coast Road.

We spent our final days at Aranga Road with Fiona’s family, staying with them until 7 November. It had been a few years since we last saw everyone, so there was certainly plenty of catching up to do. John has also done an amazing job on the house – it looks fantastic, and it was lovely to see all the improvements. 
Despite the rather uninviting grey skies, we managed a longer walk along the local beach. I had no idea it was officially called **Ripiro Beach** – to us, it had always just been the beach! It certainly has a wild character, with big whitecaps rolling in and a rather untamed feel. What I also didn't know was that Ripiro stretches for almost 100 kilometres, making it even longer than the famous 90 Mile Beach (which, rather misleadingly, is only 88 km long). You learn something new every day! 
But, as the saying goes, guests like fish start to smell after three days, so it was probably time to move on and begin our journey home. John had highly recommended stopping at Piopio Berry Orchard for their real fruit ice cream, and we weren't going to argue with that suggestion. A very worthwhile detour! 
We eventually reached our hotel in New Plymouth, rather tired and not particularly enthusiastic about hunting down a special dinner. A kebab was an easy and perfectly acceptable solution. 
The following morning, we still had one final item to tick off our wish list: the **Lake Rotokare Walkway**. What a treat! An easy but wonderfully refreshing bush walk, with a few muddy patches to keep things interesting. Definitely not one for pristine white sneakers! The real highlight, though, was stopping beside the lake and simply listening to the incredible chorus of native birds. Sometimes the best thing to do is absolutely nothing. 
Afterwards, we stopped for lunch at Windermere Berry Farm, just outside Whanganui, before making the final run to Wainuiomata. 
And just like that, our 20-day adventure came to an end. It was wonderful to be home, sleep in our own bed and unpack at last.
